newsitem.title: KENYA: Belgium hands over Rwanda genocide suspects to U.N..
newsitem.headline: Belgium hands over Rwanda genocide suspects to U.N..

text.p: Belgium has detained and transferred two former Rwandan mayors wanted by the international tribunal hunting the organisers of Rwanda's 1994 genocide, tribunal information head Beatrice Lacoste said on Monday.
Lacoste said the men -- Eli Ndayambaje and Joseph Kanyabashi -- were transferred to the U.N. detention facility in Arusha, northern Tanzania early on Saturday.

Ndayambaje was mayor of Muganza commune and Kanyabashi of Ngoma commune during the 1994 genocide by the Hutu-dominated Rwandan army and local militia groups in which up to a million Rwandans, mainly Tutsis, were slaughtered.

Lacoste said Belgium transferred the two men after receiving a formal request from the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, set up by the United Nations in late-1994 to try to bring the leaders of the genocide to justice.
The tribunal has indicted 21 people. The latest transfers bring to 14 the number now in custody. Other suspects are among Rwandan Hutu refugees in Zaire.
More than 80,000 other suspects wallow in Rwandan jails where, unlike at the tribunal, some face the death penalty.
